evidence: Plaut. Asin. 178: quasi piscis, itidemst amātor lēnae
Plaut. Pers. 2.2.61: omnēs sunt lēnae levifidae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The feminine of lēnō. In comedy she is often the girl’s mother. Cicero uses the word of anything that entices: nature is her own lēna (N. D. 1.77, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quasi piscis, itidemst amātor lēnae: nēquam est, nisi recēns
phrases.english: a lover is to a madam just what a fish is: no good unless he’s fresh

sources: Lewis & Short: lena
